They are the basic care positions in home care and community care systems.

paragraphs: The main theme of the day is "wake up, eat, take care of, and accompany": in the morning, when you arrive at the home, you first help the elderly wash and change clothes, prepare breakfast, and give medicines on time; in the morning, they clean the house and do laundry; in the afternoon, they accompany the elderly for follow-up consultations or bathing; in the evening, they write down the medication status in the nursing record, and explain a few words to the family members before driving to the next household.

In a word: pay attention to the three things of "living, caring and accompanying" in the elderly's home. Specifically, it includes assistance with eating, dressing, bathing and going to the toilet, medication reminders, turning and transferring, housework cleaning, medical accompaniment and nursing records.

Data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) show that there will be approximately 4,347,700 home health assistants employed in 2024, which is expected to rise to 5,087,500 by 2034, with a net increase of approximately 739,800 positions, an average annual vacancy of approximately 765,800, and a median annual salary of approximately US$34,900 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace home health assistants: life care is "one-on-one physical labor + emotional companionship", which requires empathy and warmth, and models cannot replace it. paragraphs: 3/10 shows that home health assistants are a care profession with "low AI exposure": process management is digitized, but the core personal care and companionship are highly dependent on people. They are a typical example of "AI helps in the background and people guard the scene", and the risk of short-term replacement is very low.

Low exposure does not mean there is no threshold: nursing is a licensed industry. If you learn skills such as disability care and rehabilitation accompaniment, and upgrade from a "nanny type" to a "professional care type", the income and service value will be completely different.

This is a career with low academic qualifications and strong employment certainty, and is suitable for children who want to be independent as soon as possible: the training and certification period for caregivers is short, and you need to gain experience first by getting a job; later, you can take the nurse qualification exam or go in the direction of rehabilitation or disability care, and the road will become wider as you go.

Learn skills such as disability care, postoperative care, and rehabilitation training, and take higher-level certificates; at the same time, learn to use nursing apps and smart devices. Once your professionalism is improved, the unit price and order quality will be significantly improved.

Nursing is one of the professions that is resistant to AI replacement, and it is not too late to change careers at the age of 40. It is recommended to take the nursing care certificate first and start with a single job from an institution or platform; highlight patience, care experience and emergency handling cases during the interview.

The nursing staff shortage is large and the turnover is fast. Retaining nursing staff relies on "insurance + skill classification + promotion channels": setting salary based on skill classification and allowing outstanding assistants to work as disabled caregivers and nursing supervisors is more cost-effective than constantly recruiting new people.
